clue.text: Ronald Harwood's kitchen piece?

definitions.meaning: Harwood's best-known play, about an old actor-manager and his valet, is called this
a piece of kitchen furniture with shelves for plates and crockery

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the title of Harwood's backstage play; the other is a sideboard with racks for displaying crockery.

clue.text: A stern uncle, say

parts.note: 'stern, say' sounds like the novelist Laurence Sterne, whose Tristram Shandy has a famously gentle uncle of this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like a description of a strict uncle, but 'say' signals a sound-alike: Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, whose kindly Uncle Toby is the reverse of stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Toby is the hobby-horse-riding old soldier in Sterne's novel Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Spy omen, perhaps, in places like Alexandria and Constantinople

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters might be put in some other order, so they are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy sees a sign of danger in old Mediterranean cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria and Constantinople were named after people, Alexander and Constantine, so each takes its name from a person.

clue.text: Henpecked and sleepy farmer from Washington (3,36)

definitions.text: Henpecked and sleepy farmer from Washington

parts.words: Henpecked and sleepy farmer from Washington
parts.note: Washington Irving's tale of a nagged Catskill farmer who sleeps for twenty years

explanation.surface: A downtrodden, drowsy farmer hails from the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' suggests the city or state; it is Washington Irving, author of the story. The '(3,36)' before the count is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving's character is bullied by his wife and dozes for twenty years in the Catskill mountains.

clue.text: Entire sort of gate from Martin Cruz Smith

definitions.meaning: an 'entire' horse is one not gelded, an uncastrated male

definitions.text: sort of gate from Martin Cruz Smith
definitions.meaning: Martin Cruz Smith wrote a novel about the atomic bomb tests named after a kind of gate

explanation.definitionFit: An entire is an ungelded male horse; Stallion Gate is Martin Cruz Smith's novel set around the Los Alamos tests.

clue.text: "Harry the king, Bedford and —" (Henry V)

parts.note: a gap to fill from the Saint Crispin's Day speech, where King Henry lists his noble companions

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Henry V with one name missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Crispin's Day speech runs 'Harry the king, Bedford and Exeter, Warwick and Talbot, Salisbury and Gloucester'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Exeter, the king's uncle, is one of the nobles named in Henry's famous rallying speech.

clue.text: Work in elevated style must be in the picture

indicators.note: the letters required are found running inside the next two words

explanation.surface: An artwork done in a lofty manner has to feature in the painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the picture' reads as a phrase about being informed; 'must be in' instead points inside 'thE PICture'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand narrative poem written in a lofty, heroic manner, like the Iliad or Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Some degree of persecution was required to make the clergy this, Swift thought

definitions.text: Some degree of persecution was required to make the clergy this, Swift thought

parts.words: Some degree of persecution was required to make the clergy this, Swift thought
parts.note: Jonathan Swift's remark that churchmen only win public favour when somewhat persecuted

explanation.surface: Jonathan Swift muses that clergymen need a little persecution.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift held that churchmen win public favour and affection only when they suffer a little.

clue.text: Holinshed history with biblical antecedent

definitions.meaning: Raphael Holinshed's Tudor history of England, Scotland and Ireland, a source for Shakespeare
two Old Testament books of this name record the history of Israel's kings

explanation.definitionFit: Holinshed's annals were titled this, and two historical books of the Old Testament share the name long before.

clue.text: Somehow stop a bloke found in private library

indicators.note: 'somehow' says the letters get there by some unstated rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Somehow you must halt a man discovered in someone's private book collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in private library' looks like the place the bloke is caught; it defines labels pasted into books.
explanation.definitionFit: Owners paste printed ex-libris labels inside the front covers of their books to mark ownership.

clue.text: Spring incitement, like fame

parts.note: Milton's Lycidas calls fame this, the goad that prompts a rider's horse to spring forward

explanation.surface: Fame acts as an incentive in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's Lycidas: 'Fame is the spur that the clear spirit doth raise.' A rider's spike makes the horse spring forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's heel spike goads a horse into action, so it stands for any incentive.

clue.text: Introverted type needs a brain stimulant?

parts.note: cerebro- is the combining form meaning brain, from Latin cerebrum
a tonic is a restorative or invigorating drink

explanation.surface: A shy person needs a pick-me-up for the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: W. H. Sheldon's body-type theory names the restrained, intellectual personality with this term.
explanation.definitionFit: In Sheldon's typology this temperament is restrained, intellectual and inward-looking, linked to a thin build.

clue.text: Vidal's Mary, quite contrary? .

indicators.note: being contrary, the name rearranges itself into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gore Vidal's Mary is being contrary, like the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' supplies the anagram signal; Vidal wrote Myra Breckinridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal's satirical novel Myra Breckinridge is named after its transgender heroine.

clue.text: … or Mary, from a well of llonelliness?

definitions.text: … or Mary, from a well of llonelliness?

parts.words: … or Mary, from a well of llonelliness?
parts.note: the Mary in Radclyffe Hall's The Well of Loneliness, the doubled l's hinting at her Welsh surname

explanation.surface: Another Mary, this one from a deep pool of solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Llewellyn is Stephen Gordon's lover in Radclyffe Hall's novel; the misspelling 'llonelliness' imitates the Welsh double L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Llewellyn is the young Welsh woman loved by Stephen Gordon in Radclyffe Hall's novel.

clue.text: Olivia Manning's distinctive face

parts.note: Manning wrote a novel titled with these words before 'Face'

explanation.surface: The novelist Olivia Manning had striking features.
explanation.walkthrough: Manning's 1957 novel is A Different Face; 'distinctive' clues the two words before 'Face'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manning's novel title opens with these two words, and 'distinctive' means set apart or unlike others.

clue.text: Family in Devonshire displaying both reason and emotion between the covers

definitions.text: Family in Devonshire displaying both reason and emotion between the covers

parts.words: Family in Devonshire displaying both reason and emotion between the covers
parts.note: the family who move to Devon in Austen's Sense and Sensibility, a book showing good sense and feeling

explanation.surface: A Devon household shows both head and heart in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reason and emotion' is Sense and Sensibility, and 'between the covers' means in a book, not in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor and Marianne's family move to Barton Cottage in Devon in Jane Austen's novel.

clue.text: Scott's "proud, fierce, jealous and irritable" Saxon

definitions.text: Scott's "proud, fierce, jealous and irritable" Saxon

parts.words: Scott's "proud, fierce, jealous and irritable" Saxon
parts.note: Walter Scott's description of the Saxon thane in Ivanhoe, father of the hero

explanation.surface: Walter Scott sketches a hot-tempered Anglo-Saxon nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedric the Saxon, Ivanhoe's father, is the stubborn thane of Rotherwood in Scott's novel.

clue.text: Roderick Alleyn investigated one to death

definitions.text: Roderick Alleyn investigated one to death

parts.words: Roderick Alleyn investigated one to death
parts.note: Ngaio Marsh's detective Alleyn solves a case in a novel whose title runs '... to Death'

explanation.surface: A detective looked into something until it died.
explanation.walkthrough: Ngaio Marsh's novel Overture to Death features Inspector Roderick Alleyn; 'one' stands for the first word of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh's Overture to Death has a murder at a village concert, where an opening piece is played.

clue.text: Anita Brookner's was from England

parts.note: Brookner wrote a novel titled 'A ... from England'

explanation.surface: Anita Brookner's someone came from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Brookner's 1987 novel is A Friend from England, about a lonely woman's attachment to a family.

clue.text: Produced by a swinger in church

definitions.text: Produced by a swinger in church

parts.words: Produced by a swinger in church
parts.note: a censer swung on chains during a service gives off fragrant smoke

explanation.surface: Something made by a promiscuous person at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinger' suggests a promiscuous partygoer; it is a thurible swung during worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic resin burned in a thurible gives the perfumed smoke used in church worship.

clue.text: Exaggerated character from Measure for Measure?

definitions.meaning: Mistress ... is the bawd in Shakespeare's play

explanation.definitionFit: Something laid on too thick is overstated; Mistress Overdone keeps a brothel in Shakespeare's Vienna.

clue.text: In Harrington's Commonwealth I reveal South Sea islands

indicators.note: 'In' puts the I among the letters of the Commonwealth's name

parts.note: James Harrington's 1656 utopia is The Commonwealth of Oceana

explanation.surface: In a utopian commonwealth I reveal the Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: James Harrington (1611-77) wrote the political utopia The Commonwealth of Oceana; I goes inside that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective name for the Pacific island groups, Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia, with Australasia.

clue.text: "If any man that which he merits /Or any merit that which he —s" (Coleridge)

definitions.text: "If any man that which he merits /Or any merit that which he —s" (Coleridge)

parts.words: "If any man that which he merits /Or any merit that which he —s" (Coleridge)
parts.note: a gap from Coleridge's epigram, meaning to gain or get

explanation.surface: A Coleridge couplet on merit with its last verb missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to gain or get, completing Coleridge's play on 'merits' and 'merit'.

clue.text: Weapon of former bore, reportedly

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: 'reportedly' says the word for bore is heard, not spelt

parts.note: the bore of a gun is its calibre

explanation.surface: A weapon owned by a dull ex, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the inside width of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's sword, drawn from the stone or given by the Lady of the Lake.

clue.text: Those other film-star workers

definitions.meaning: people other than us, as a pronoun
the 1954 film ...! stars giant mutant worker ants

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for other people; the 1954 film Them! features giant radioactive worker ants.

clue.text: Philosophical being saved from useless effort

indicators.note: the letters are rescued from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Philosophy's existence rescued from wasted effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin 'to be', used by philosophers for existence or essential nature.

clue.text: Dame reminiscent of Miss Ferber

definitions.meaning: Dame ... Everage, Barry Humphries's stage character
the novelist ... Ferber wrote Show Boat and Giant

explanation.definitionFit: Barry Humphries's character Dame Edna Everage shares a first name with the American novelist Edna Ferber.

clue.text: Gloomy and taciturn Shakespearean emperor

parts.note: the Roman emperor in Titus Andronicus, whose name suggests a sullen, saturnine temper

explanation.surface: A moody, silent emperor from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloomy and taciturn' means saturnine, which suggests the emperor's name in Titus Andronicus.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturninus is the Roman emperor in Titus Andronicus; 'saturnine' means sullen and morose.

clue.text: Half-brother of Sir Max (the acting branch)

definitions.text: Half-brother of Sir Max (the acting branch)

parts.words: Half-brother of Sir Max (the acting branch)
parts.note: Sir Max Beerbohm's half-brother was the actor-manager Herbert Beerbohm, and the word also means a branching plant

explanation.surface: The theatrical side of Sir Max Beerbohm's family.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree, actor-manager, was Max Beerbohm's half-brother; 'branch' plays on the family tree and on wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the actor-manager, was Max Beerbohm's half-brother; a family branch grows on a trunk.

clue.text: He could have made a cleaner gal. But not of Tess (55)

definitions.text: He could have made a cleaner gal. But not of Tess

indicators.note: the letters are made into a man's name by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who might have turned a girl spotless, except in Hardy's Tess.
explanation.walkthrough: Angel Clare marries Tess in Hardy's novel but deserts her on learning her past, so he never 'made her clean'. The '(55)' is a print slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel Clare is the parson's son who marries and then abandons Tess in Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles.
